answer.evidence: `_find` in radon/raw.py:72-79 iterates `enumerate(reversed(tokens))` and compares `(token, value)` with `token_values[:2]`. On the first hit it returns `len(tokens) - index - 1`, which maps the reversed index back to the original index of the rightmost match. If no token matches, the loop ends and it raises `ValueError('(token, value) pair not found')`. Review points: `tokens` must be a sequence, because `reversed` fails on a generator, and the sibling `_split_tokens` has the same pair-comparison shape. I'd spend the most time checking how callers of `_find` handle the ValueError, and whether radon/metrics.py and radon/visitors.py do similar token or pair lookups with different not-found behavior. radon/complexity.py gets a shorter pass for consistency of its error handling.
